name: Selkup
notes: Northern (Taz) Selkup, Samoyedic branch, Yamalo-Nenets/Tomsk region, Russia. INPUT CONTRACT: Northern Selkup Cyrillic orthography (Cyrillicised script standardised on the Taz dialect), NFC. ⟨ӧ⟩ and ⟨ө⟩ are both attested spellings of the same front rounded vowel /ø/ across Selkup pedagogical materials (Helimski 1998; Kuznetsova et al.). Consonants palatalise before the iotated vowels ⟨е и ю я⟩ and the soft sign ⟨ь⟩ (Helimski 1998; directly evidenced by NorthEuraLex тимы -> tʲ i m ɨ and пептай -> pʲ e p t a j), so those sequences are entered as multigraph keys the maximal-munch matcher prefers over the bare consonant. Consonant length is contrastive and spelled by doubling the letter, e.g. ⟨тт⟩ /tː/ (NorthEuraLex өӈыттоп -> ø ŋ ɨ tː o p) — its IPA is not the concatenation of two /t/ onsets, it is one long stop. Selkup additionally distinguishes phonemic vowel length (Helimski 1998), but this dataset's available primary sources do not give a citable spelling convention for long vowels beyond consonant gemination, so vowel length is NOT modelled here (ENGINE-LIMIT / sourcing gap, documented rather than guessed). Word stress in Northern Selkup interacts with vowel quantity and is not simply orthography-predictable (Helimski 1998); documented here as an ENGINE-LIMIT stress exemption and not modelled. ITERATION FIX (error-analysis pass against NorthEuraLex): ⟨а⟩ corrected to plain /a/ (not /ä/, NorthEuraLex тама -> tama, амна -> amna); the ⟨н⟩/⟨л⟩ palatalisation series corrected from the /nʲ/ /lʲ/ sequences to the fused palatals /ɲ/ /ʎ/ that NorthEuraLex's transcription consistently shows (нюня -> ɲuɲa, лем -> ʎem); and ⟨ще⟩/⟨щё⟩ entered as multigraphs /ɕe/ /ɕo/ so the iotated [j]-initial reading of the base vowel letter does not intrude after this already-palatal fricative (NorthEuraLex ще -> ɕe). Classification and coordinates follow Glottolog.
